# Evening hours at the tool library: a 12-week pilot

*An invented document, written only to exercise the render checks. No organisation, person or
figure in it is real.*

**The answer.** Open the tool library three evenings a week for 12 weeks, on a budget of $18K, and
hire one paid coordinator at 20 hours a week. The one decision that cannot wait is the hire.

## Where things stand

- 140 of 420 members asked for evening hours in the autumn survey.
- 0 evening visits today: the library closes at 17:00.
- 9 volunteers have signed up for evening shifts; a three-evening week needs 12.

## The plan

| Weeks | Evenings open | Staffed by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1–4 | 2 a week | volunteers and the coordinator |
| 5–12 | 3 a week | volunteers and the coordinator |

The coordinator starts in week 1. Weeks 1 to 4 test the rota on two evenings before the third is
added.

## The money

$18K for the pilot. Most of it pays the coordinator: 20 hours a week for 12 weeks is 240 hours,
about $14K. The rest, about $4K, covers lighting, a second key-safe and a printed rota.

## What it will not tell us

Whether evening members borrow differently from daytime members. That needs a full term of loan
records, so week 12 at the earliest.

## The decision

**Hire one coordinator at 20 hours a week, or run the pilot on volunteers alone?** Recommended:
hire. With 9 of the 12 shifts covered, a volunteer-only rota leaves one evening in four unstaffed.
